concepts.why: The patient presented with acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain and was found to have a perforated appendix with surrounding fat stranding on CT scan.
The patient has a history of prostate cancer in remission and was found to have innumerable hepatic nodules and bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy, suggesting metastatic disease.

The patient was found to have mural thickening of the cecum and sigmoid colon, and a thickened, woody sigmoid colon was noted during exploratory laparotomy, suggesting a possible colorectal malignancy.
The patient was found to have pulmonary consolidation and collapse in the right lower lobe, and developed respiratory failure, suggesting a possible pneumonia.
The patient presented with fever, hypotension, and tachycardia, and had a perforated appendix with peritonitis, suggesting sepsis.

rationales.F05: Prostate cancer in remission increases the likelihood of metastatic prostate cancer.
rationales.F06: Acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain is a common symptom of acute appendicitis.
rationales.F10: Perforated appendix is a definitive diagnosis of acute appendicitis.
rationales.F11: Innumerable hepatic nodules suggest metastatic disease, which could be from prostate cancer or colorectal cancer.
rationales.F12: Bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy is concerning for metastatic disease, which could be from prostate cancer or colorectal cancer.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient presented with febrile, hypotensive, and tachycardic symptoms, which are classic signs of sepsis, and had a clear source of infection with a perforated appendix, making sepsis the most fitting diagnosis.
